title: Policy + autoscaler audit log event shape (notes) — Dedicated autoscaling bounds
content:
Context
- Project: Dedicated autoscaling policies with customer bounds (min/max) + predictive scaling.
- Enterprise asks: “who changed bounds, when, what exactly changed, and what did the autoscaler do as a result?”
- This doc is a working note for event shapes needed for compliance reviews, customer audit requests, and internal incident debugging.

Non-goals
- Not defining the full storage/retention backend (separate doc / Kevin).
- Not defining metrics naming (see metric naming standards doc).

Principles / requirements
1) Deterministic and explainable
- For every autoscaler loop decision, record both:
  a) requested_desired (from reactive + predictive arbitration), and
  b) bounded_desired (after applying min/max + safety invariants)
- Record “why” at a human-auditable level (reason codes + top inputs).

2) Minimal sensitive data
- Do not log prompts, payloads, or customer data.
- Avoid embedding full config objects if it creates risk; include diffs and/or hashed snapshots where feasible.

3) Correlatable
- Every event includes correlation IDs (request_id, trace_id if available) and stable identifiers (account_id, deployment_id, region).
- Autoscaler decision events should link back to the policy revision used.

4) Compliance-friendly
- Include actor identity for config changes (user/service principal), RBAC role, and source channel (Console/API/Terraform).
- Immutability expectations: audit logs are append-only; updates are new events.

5) Cardinality control
- Avoid high-cardinality labels beyond account_id/deployment_id/region.
- For signals (queue depth, utilization), include a small set of numeric summaries, not per-node details.


Event envelope (common fields)
All audit events emitted by Control Plane + Autoscaler should share a standard envelope.

Required envelope fields
- event_name: string (e.g., "dedicated.scaling_policy.updated")
- event_version: string (e.g., "1.0")
- event_id: string UUID (unique per event)
- emitted_at: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
- severity: string (INFO|WARN|ERROR)
- environment: string (prod|staging)
- region: string (e.g., "us-east-1")
- account_id: string
- deployment_id: string
- dedicated_pool_id: string (if applicable)
- source: string (control-plane|autoscaler|console-backend|terraform-provider)
- actor_type: string (human|service)
- actor_id: string (user_id or service_principal_id)
- actor_email: string (optional; include only if already stored in audit systems; confirm with Security)
- actor_roles: string (comma-separated roles at time of action; snapshot)
- ip_address: string (optional; for human changes via Console/API)
- user_agent: string (optional)
- request_id: string (API request id)
- trace_id: string (if available)

Recommended envelope fields
- org_id: string (if different from account_id in enterprise multi-org)
- workspace_id: string (Console workspace)
- customer_ticket_ref: string (e.g., "SUP-28411" if change was done as a support action)
- related_event_ids: string (comma-separated event_ids for linking, e.g., decision -> prior policy update)


Policy change events (Control Plane)

1) dedicated.scaling_policy.updated
When
- Any update to scaling policy for a Dedicated deployment (min/max, cooldowns, predictive settings, etc.)

Event-specific fields (in addition to envelope)
- policy_id: string
- policy_revision: string (monotonic int stored as string)
- update_channel: string (console|api|terraform|internal-admin)
- change_type: string (create|update|delete)
- validation_result: string (accepted|rejected)
- previous_policy_revision: string (empty if create)

Config diff fields (compliance-friendly)
- changed_fields: string (comma-separated list; e.g., "min_replicas,max_replicas,predictive_mode")
- previous_values: string (redacted summary; see below)
- new_values: string (redacted summary; see below)

Recommended representation for previous_values/new_values
- Keep as a compact key=value list (not raw JSON object), e.g.:
  "min_replicas=8; max_replicas=40; cooldown_up_s=60; cooldown_down_s=300; predictive_mode=enabled; predictive_lead_time_s=600"
- For future: include policy_snapshot_hash (sha256) and store full snapshot in a secured config store if we need it.

Additional fields needed for reviews
- approval_required: string (true|false)
- approval_status: string (not_required|pending|approved|denied)
- approver_actor_id: string (if applicable)
- justification: string (free-text, required for internal-admin changes)


2) dedicated.scaling_policy.update_rejected
When
- Policy update attempt fails validation or RBAC.

Event-specific fields
- policy_id: string (if exists)
- attempted_fields: string (comma-separated)
- rejection_reason_code: string (rbac_denied|min_gt_max|cooldown_invalid|predictive_not_enabled_for_account|rate_limited|unknown)
- rejection_details: string (human readable; must not include secrets)

Notes
- We should emit this even on 4xx responses from API to support compliance: “attempted change was rejected.”


3) dedicated.scaling_policy.rate_limited
When
- Excessive config churn protection triggers (see PR-48333).

Event-specific fields
- limit_name: string (e.g., "scaling_policy_updates_per_hour")
- limit_value: string (e.g., "10")
- window_s: string
- current_count: string
- action_taken: string (blocked|allowed_with_warning)


Autoscaler decision events (Fleet/Infra)

4) dedicated.autoscaler.decision_made
When
- Each autoscaler evaluation loop when a decision is computed (even if it results in no scaling action).

Event-specific fields
- autoscaler_instance_id: string (for debugging)
- evaluation_id: string (uuid for this loop)
- policy_id: string
- policy_revision: string (the exact revision used)
- mode: string (reactive|predictive|predictive_with_reactive_override)

Inputs summary (keep small)
- current_replicas: string
- requested_desired_replicas: string (pre-bounds)
- bounded_desired_replicas: string (post-bounds)
- action: string (scale_up|scale_down|no_change)
- step_applied: string (e.g., "+4" or "-2" or "0")
- cooldown_state: string (ok|in_cooldown_up|in_cooldown_down)

Reasoning fields
- primary_reason_code: string (queue_depth_high|utilization_high|prediction_ramp|max_bound_reached|min_bound_enforced|forecast_stale|insufficient_capacity|safety_baseline|error)
- contributing_reason_codes: string (comma-separated)

Signals snapshot (numeric summaries)
- queue_depth_p95: string
- queue_wait_ms_p95: string
- gpu_utilization_avg: string
- tokens_per_s_per_replica_est: string (if available)
- saturation_score: string (0-1)

Predictive fields (only when predictive enabled)
- forecast_id: string
- forecast_generated_at: string (RFC3339)
- forecast_horizon_s: string
- forecast_value_rps: string
- forecast_confidence: string (0-1 or categorical: low|med|high)
- prediction_error_recent: string (optional: MAPE over last N minutes)
- forecast_staleness_s: string

Operational fields
- capacity_shortage: string (true|false)
- shortage_reason: string (region_out_of_capacity|instance_type_unavailable|quota_limited|unknown)
- bounded_state: string (none|min_enforced|max_enforced|min_unmet)


5) dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit
When
- requested_desired_replicas is clamped by min/max, OR min cannot be met due to region shortage.

Event-specific fields
- bound_type: string (min|max|min_unmet)
- bound_value: string
- requested_desired_replicas: string
- bounded_desired_replicas: string
- duration_s: string (if emitted as periodic summary; otherwise empty)
- customer_impact_risk: string (low|medium|high)

Note
- This is important for enterprise: proves we never exceeded max, and shows when max is the limiting factor for latency.


6) dedicated.autoscaler.forecast_unavailable
When
- Predictive mode is enabled but forecast provider returns null/stale/outage; autoscaler falls back.

Event-specific fields
- forecast_provider: string
- failure_mode: string (null_response|timeout|stale|bad_schema)
- fallback_action: string (use_reactive|hold_last_forecast|disable_predictive_temporarily)
- hold_last_forecast_age_s: string (if applicable)


7) dedicated.autoscaler.scale_action_applied
When
- Actual change requested to the fleet orchestrator (vs decision computation).

Event-specific fields
- evaluation_id: string
- previous_replicas: string
- new_replicas: string
- orchestrator_request_id: string
- outcome: string (success|failed|partial)
- failure_reason: string (if failed)

Why separate decision vs action?
- Decision events answer “what should we do?”
- Action events answer “did we do it?” (and gives correlation to provisioning).


Console / Admin actions (optional but recommended)

8) dedicated.scaling_policy.viewed
When
- An admin/support user views a policy in internal admin tools.

Event-specific fields
- view_channel: string (console|admin_cli)
- purpose: string (support|security_review|customer_request|unknown)

Note
- Might be overkill; confirm with Security/Compliance whether access logging is required.


Redaction + data handling notes
- Do not include customer names; use account_id.
- Do not include full Kubernetes object dumps, node IDs, or per-replica metrics.
- Keep “previous_values/new_values” compact and strictly limited to the scaling policy surface.
- For internal-admin operations, justification should be required; for automated operations (autoscaler), justification is via reason codes.


Schema versioning
- event_version is required and must be bumped on any breaking change.
- Prefer additive changes only (new fields) in v1.
- If we need to change meaning of a field, add a new field and deprecate the old one.


Example events (textual)

Example A — policy updated via Terraform
- event_name: dedicated.scaling_policy.updated
- source: terraform-provider
- actor_type: service
- actor_id: spn_terraform_9d2...
- account_id: acct_4b1...
- deployment_id: dep_dedicated_7f1...
- changed_fields: min_replicas,max_replicas,predictive_mode
- previous_values: min_replicas=6; max_replicas=24; predictive_mode=disabled
- new_values: min_replicas=10; max_replicas=24; predictive_mode=enabled; predictive_lead_time_s=900
- approval_required: false

Example B — autoscaler clamps at max
- event_name: dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit
- bound_type: max
- bound_value: 24
- requested_desired_replicas: 31
- bounded_desired_replicas: 24
- primary_reason_code: max_bound_reached
- queue_wait_ms_p95: 2200
- capacity_shortage: false

Example C — min unmet due to region shortage
- event_name: dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit
- bound_type: min_unmet
- bound_value: 16
- requested_desired_replicas: 16
- bounded_desired_replicas: 12
- capacity_shortage: true
- shortage_reason: region_out_of_capacity


Open questions / follow-ups
1) actor_email in audit logs
- Security preference: store actor_id and resolve email in Console for display vs emitting email in the event.
- Action: Marcus/Naomi to confirm compliance requirements.

2) Retention and customer export
- Enterprise asks vary (90 days, 180 days, 1 year+). We should align on default retention tiers.
- Action: Kevin to propose retention by plan + export to SIEM.

3) Volume concerns
- decision_made emitted every loop might be high volume.
  Options:
  a) emit decision_made only when action != no_change OR bounded_state != none
  b) emit decision_made sampled (e.g., 1/10) + always emit bound_hit/scale_action_applied
- Action: Rafael + Vanessa to weigh debugging value vs cost.

4) Linking to customer-facing “Scaling History” view
- Console wants a “Scaling Events” timeline with reasons.
- Need stable reason codes and human-friendly mapping.
- Action: Felix to define UI mapping + filtering (bound hits, forecast unavailable, scale actions).

5) Approval workflows
- Some customers may request “4-eyes” for max bound increases.
- Not in initial scope, but audit schema should not block it.
- Action: Lauren to confirm if this is on roadmap; if yes, include approval_* fields now (optional).
